en.name: Basil, fresh
en.summary: Fresh basil keeps 5 days at room temperature with its stems in water, or 10 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it will start to discolour. It is the one common herb that is often happier on the counter than in the cold.
en.pantry: 5 days with the stems in water, like a bouquet, somewhere out of direct sun. Trim the ends, stand them in an inch of clean water, change the water daily and do not cover the leaves — basil wants air around it. This is a genuinely useful option because basil is chilling-sensitive: the leaves blacken at cold temperatures in a way that mint and parsley do not. A bunch on the worktop in a glass looks after itself, and you pick from it as you cook.
en.fridge: 10 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and expect it to start discolouring — dark patches and blackened edges are cold injury rather than rot. If you are refrigerating it, wrap the bunch loosely in dry kitchen paper inside an open or perforated bag and put it in the warmest part of the fridge, usually the door or the top shelf. Do not wash it until you are about to use it; wet basil leaves collapse into slime within a day.
en.freezer: Freezing whole basil leaves is disappointing — they blacken and go limp, though the flavour largely survives. The method that does work is to blitz the leaves with olive oil and freeze the paste in an ice-cube tray, or to freeze finished pesto; the oil protects the leaf from the cold and from the air, and a cube goes straight into a sauce.
en.thawing: Use basil-and-oil cubes straight from frozen, dropped into a hot pan or a warm sauce. Do not thaw whole leaves and expect to garnish with them.
spoilage: Blackened, translucent leaves that have gone slimy.
A sour or fermented smell instead of a sweet, peppery one.
Slime at the cut ends or in the water in the glass.
Mould on the stems, particularly where they sat in stale water.
tips: Stand the bunch in water on the counter rather than putting it in the fridge.
Change the water every day and re-trim the stems.
Do not wash the leaves until you use them.
Tear rather than chop, and add it at the very end of cooking.

faq.q: How long does fresh basil keep?
faq.a: 5 days at room temperature with the stems in water, or 10 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it will start to discolour.

faq.q: Why does basil turn black in the fridge?
faq.a: It is chilling-sensitive. Cold damages the leaf cells, which is why a glass of water on the counter often keeps it looking better than the fridge does.
Whole leaves blacken and go limp. Blitz the leaves with olive oil and freeze the paste in cubes instead, or freeze finished pesto.

zh.name: 新鮮羅勒
zh.summary: 新鮮羅勒把莖泡在水裡放常溫可放 5 天，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 10 天，但會開始變色。它是少數幾種「放在檯面上往往比放冰箱開心」的常見香草。
zh.pantry: 把莖插在水裡、像一束花那樣放在不直曬的地方，5 天。請先剪掉末端，插進約 2 到 3 公分深的乾淨水中，每天換水，葉子不要蓋起來——羅勒需要周圍有空氣。這個做法是真的有用，因為羅勒怕冷：它的葉子在低溫下會發黑，而薄荷和巴西利不會。一束插在玻璃杯裡的羅勒幾乎不用照顧，煮菜時隨手摘。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 10 天，而且要有心理準備它會開始變色——深色斑塊和發黑的葉緣是冷害，不是腐爛。要冷藏的話，請用乾的廚房紙巾把整束鬆鬆地包起來，裝進敞口或打洞的袋子，放冰箱最不冷的位置，通常是門邊或上層。不要提早洗；濕掉的羅勒葉一天之內就會爛成一團黏泥。
zh.freezer: 整片羅勒葉冷凍的結果很令人失望——會發黑、變軟塌，雖然風味大致還在。真正可行的方法是把葉子和橄欖油一起打成泥、用製冰盒冷凍，或直接冷凍做好的青醬；油會同時擋掉低溫與空氣，一塊直接丟進醬汁就好。
zh.thawing: 羅勒油醬冰塊直接從冷凍取用，丟進熱鍋或溫熱的醬汁裡。不要期待整片葉子解凍後還能拿來擺盤。
spoilage: 葉子發黑、變透明、摸起來黏滑。
聞起來酸或有發酵味，而不是帶胡椒感的清甜香。
莖的切口或杯子裡的水變得黏滑。
莖上長霉，特別是泡在放久的水裡的那一段。
tips: 整束插水放檯面上，比放冰箱好。
每天換水，並重新剪一下莖。
用手撕不要用刀切，而且起鍋前才放。

faq.a: 莖插水放常溫 5 天，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 10 天，但冷藏會開始變色。

faq.q: 羅勒為什麼放冰箱會變黑？
faq.a: 它怕冷。低溫會傷害葉片細胞，這也是為什麼插在水杯裡放檯面上，常常看起來比冰箱裡好。
整片葉子會發黑變軟。請改成把葉子和橄欖油打成泥、分塊冷凍，或直接冷凍做好的青醬。
